messages:
maria: quick heads-up — we need to revisit the admission control for us-east-1 GPU pools. over the last 72h we've seen sustained saturation and downstream region spillovers causing p99 latency SLO misses and a ~6% cross-region egress cost bump :grimacing:
ken: can you paste the numbers? is this from the canary change last night?
sudha: I saw the alert too, looks like queues grew then we started dropping at 95th percentile of connection count. link: https://grafana.redwood/infraprod/d/sat/fleet-sat
maria: metrics snapshot (last 72h):
```
- GPU util p95: 92%
- queue_depth_avg: 18 -> 42
- soft_degrade_rate: 0.8% (was 0.3%)
- hard_reject_rate: 0.1% (spiked at 0.9% during warmup)
- cross_region_egress_delta: +6.1% (~$18k/mo)
- p99-gen-latency: 1.9s -> 3.6s for tail users (us-east->eu fallback)
```
dave: that fallback pattern (us-east -> eu) is the killer — latency + cost + customer complaints. What's the proposed policy change?
maria: options on the table: 1) raise hard reject threshold (reject earlier), 2) widen degrade window (more soft-degrades with lower token budgets), 3) dynamic queue with per-customer priority + short-circuit fallback to CPU-only path. plus a hybrid: rate-limit low-priority traffic earlier and keep high-priority warm pools.
alisha: preference: avoid customer-visible rejects for paid tiers. soft-degrade + priority queue for free-tier traffic seems better. but needs careful backpressure so we don't keep queueing forever and trigger cross-region spill.
ken: can we do a short token-bucket throttle at the edge (gateway) so we never route >X rps to a region? that prevents spillover.
sudha: yes — we can add a region-capacity guard in the router (pseudo):
```
if region_available_slots < threshold:
  if request.priority == "free": return soft_degrade()
  else: route_to_local_warmpool_or_cpu_fallback()
```
ken: curious about impact on unit cost. soft-degrade still consumes tokens on GPU but fewer steps; cpu-fallback uses no GPU but worse latency. need numbers.
maria: quick cost model rough:
```
- GPU token cost per 1m tokens: $0.6
- CPU fallback cost per 1m tokens: $0.15
- customer-churn risk if p99 > 5s: high
```
so pure reject reduces cost but increases churn risk. soft-degrade trades quality for cost and is safer for paid users if tiered.
dave: what about queue length cap + eviction policy? e.g., cap queue at 1000 across region, evict oldest free-tier requests with a 503 after warmbackoff. keeps tail bounded.
alisha: evicting oldest may penalize long-running customer requests. prefer priority-based eviction (LRU-ish by session age + tier).
infra-bot: deployment checklist for policy flip: canary config -> 10% traffic -> monitor p99 latency, reject rate, cross-region egress -> rollback window 30m.
sudha: I sketched a canary config (gateway flag):
```
policy: "tiered-softfail"
params:
  region_threshold_pct: 88
  queue_cap: 1200
  soft_degrade: true
  degrade_budget_tokens: 0.6
  evict_policy: "tiered_oldest_first"
  route_block_egress: true
```
ken: propose we run two experiments: A) aggressive early-reject (reduce queue cap to 200, reject free-tier) B) tiered-softfail (cap 1200 + degrade) — run A on a non-critical zone and B on us-east canary. compare churn proxy + egress delta + p99.
maria: timeline: roll B (tiered-softfail) to 5% traffic in us-east tonight, monitor 6h, if p99 improves and egress drops -> 25% -> 2h -> full. rollback if user-error-rate or p99 worsens.
dave: add synthetic customer probes that hit long sequences to ensure we don't silently degrade paid sessions.
alisha: I'll update the ops runbook with the evict rules + SLA mappings.
ken: can we have a temporary billing credit if we detect customers routed cross-region due to our fallback? ops/legal might require that.
maria: good call — i'll loop in customer-success after canary results.
infra-bot: scheduled: canary rollout (tiered-softfail) in us-east at 22:00 UTC | timeout window 30m | notify #incidents on rollback.
ken: ack. I'll own monitoring dashboards and alert thresholds for tonight.
sudha: I'll push the router flag + unit tests in PR #4521, ETA 3h.
maria: thanks team — goal is to avoid hard rejects for paid users while bounding tail costs and stopping cross-region spill. will report back after first canary. :thumbsup:
